ideas.title: Return policy replies

ideas.title: Calm words for an upset customer

ideas.title: A text asking to swap a shift
ideas.why: Helps you ask your manager politely without overthinking it.
ideas.prompt: Write a short text from me to my manager asking to swap my shift on [day] because of [reason]. Be polite and clear in three sentences or fewer, and offer to cover [other day] if that helps. Sound like a friendly coworker, not formal.

ideas.title: Easy dinners after a long shift
ideas.why: Gives you tired day meal ideas that don’t take much effort.
ideas.prompt: I’m on my feet all day as a cashier and I get home tired around [time]. Give me five dinner ideas I can make with [ingredients I have on hand] with little effort and little cleanup. Write a short list with a one line how to for each. Keep it simple and don’t give diet advice.

ideas.title: A plan for a free weekend
ideas.why: Turns a rare day off into a plan so it doesn’t slip away.
ideas.prompt: I have a free [Saturday or Sunday] after a lot of shifts. Plan a relaxed day for me in [my town] with a budget of [amount]. Give me a morning, afternoon and evening idea, mostly low cost, plus one backup idea in case of rain. Keep it short and easy to read.

safeUse: Read and check everything before it goes out or you say it to a customer.

Ask your manager which AI tools are approved before using AI on anything from work.

plan.toolWhy: You said you’d most like help with replying to customer messages, especially the size and hold DMs that eat your afternoon. ChatGPT is a good place to start because the free version is enough to begin, it works in a browser or a phone app, and you type to it like a text message.

yourTools.name: Instagram
yourTools.what: Instagram is where many of your size and hold questions land, and it’s also where your captions go. You can write replies and captions in ChatGPT, then paste them in.
yourTools.tryThis: This week, paste a few DMs you get most often into ChatGPT, with names left out, and ask for a short reply for each. Save the ones you like in a note to copy from.
yourTools.withChat: Draft the reply in ChatGPT and ask for two tones, friendly and quick. Then paste your pick into Instagram and add the real size or hold details yourself.

yourTools.name: Texts
yourTools.what: Texts are a quick way to answer customers who already have your number, and to reach your part timers. Short, clear replies work best there.
yourTools.tryThis: Ask ChatGPT to turn a long hold reply into a text of two sentences, then keep it as your go to version.
yourTools.withChat: Paste the customer’s question into ChatGPT with no name or number. Ask for a text reply under 40 words, then check it and send it from your phone.

yourTools.name: Square
yourTools.what: Square holds your sales and item information, so it’s a good place to check what’s really in stock before you reply. Some Square tools may have AI features, and some may need a paid plan.
yourTools.tryThis: Look in Square for an item or inventory view and see if it helps you confirm a size before you answer. Then use ChatGPT only for the wording.
yourTools.withChat: Check the size in Square first. Then ask ChatGPT to write the reply using the facts you give it, and read it before sending.
